title: UcDocument
description: A complete use-case document (YAML frontmatter + Cockburn-template body), derived directly from `uc_reference_mdformat.md`/`uc_reference_mdformat.ast` (the mdformat-normalized reference document and its CommonMark AST dump) rather than from source code. Property names/nesting mirror `src/biz/dfch/specmgr/uc/models/v2/use_case.py`, `frontmatter.py`, `document.py` (the `models/md`-engine-backed Pydantic models), including the three heading/field-naming mismatches this schema originally surfaced (`Preconditions`, `Channels to Primary/Secondary Actors`, frontmatter `type`) -- all three have since been reconciled, in the document's favor for the first two (the model's `Precondition`/`ChannelsToPrimaryActor`/`ChannelsToSecondaryActors` classes now declare an explicit `@alias` matching the document's own heading text) and in the model's favor for the third (the reference document's frontmatter now reads `type: uc`, not `type: doc-uc`). As with `v1/uc_schema.json`, cross-field/cross-item invariants (e.g. `UseCase.validate_step_references_resolve_and_are_unique`) cannot be expressed in JSON Schema draft-07 and are enforced by `model_validator`s instead -- this schema documents field shape/format only. Frontmatter stripping is not this schema's concern either (same `models/md` REQ-003 convention as the Pydantic models): a conforming document's `---...---` YAML block is parsed separately from the body.

frontmatter.description: YAML frontmatter metadata, parsed independently of the CommonMark body (see `models.md.MarkdownFrontmatter`/`uc.models.v2.UcFrontmatter`). Never itself part of the document's AST -- `uc_reference_mdformat.ast`'s leading `thematic_break`/`heading` nodes are an artifact of dumping the AST *without* first stripping the `---...---` block (see `uc_reference.md`'s literal frontmatter for the actual source of truth used here).

id.description: Specmgr-assigned document identifier. Optional; `null`/absent for a not-yet-registered, hand-authored document. Unlike `uc/models/v1`, no `^uc-[0-9]+$` pattern is enforced -- any string is accepted (see `UcFrontmatter`'s own docstring). Reference document value: "uc-001".

type.description: Document-type discriminator. Fixed to "uc", matching `UcFrontmatter.type: Literal["uc"] = "uc"`.

version.description: The `models.md` schema major.minor.patch version this frontmatter was written with.

created.description: Free-form date/timestamp the document was first created (not format-validated -- `models.md.MarkdownFrontmatter.created` is a plain optional string). Reference document value: "2026-08-05T08:15:42".

updated.description: Free-form date/timestamp the document was last updated (not format-validated). Reference document value: "2026-08-06T03:27:27".

title.description: Use case name, from the document's single H1 heading.

characteristic_information.description: Body of the H2 'Characteristic Information' section. Every h3 sub-field is modeled as `list[MarkdownParagraph]` ('body' shape, prose) or `list[MarkdownListItem]` ('items' shape, bullet list) on the corresponding v2 class -- represented uniformly below as a JSON array of strings, one entry per paragraph/list item (almost always length 1 for the 'body'-shaped fields in practice).

goal_in_context.description: H3 'Goal in Context'. Longer statement of the goal in context, if needed.

scope.description: H3 'Scope'. What system is being considered as a black box under design.

level.description: H3 'Level'. Scope level of the use case (e.g. 'Summary', 'Primary task', 'Subfunction' -- not enforced as an enum by the v2 model, unlike v1's JSON Schema).

preconditions.description: H3 'Preconditions'. What we expect is already the state of the world. `uc.models.v2.use_case.Preconditions` (renamed from the singular `Precondition`) derives this exact heading from its own class name -- no explicit `@alias` needed.

success_end_condition.description: H3 'Success End Condition'. The state of the world upon successful completion.

failed_end_condition.description: H3 'Failed End Condition' (optional). The state of the world if the goal is abandoned.

primary_actor.description: H3 'Primary Actor'. A role name for the primary actor, or a description.

secondary_actors.description: H3 'Secondary Actors' (optional). Other systems/actors needed to accomplish the use case.

trigger.description: H3 'Trigger'. The action upon the system that starts the use case (may be a time event).

frequency.description: H3 'Frequency' (optional). How often the use case is expected to happen (e.g. '200 per day').

priority.description: H3 'Priority' (optional). How critical this use case is to the system/organization.

performance_target.description: H3 'Performance Target' (optional). The amount of time this use case should take.

channels_to_primary_actor.description: H3 'Channels to Primary Actor' (optional). How the primary actor interacts with the system. `uc.models.v2.use_case.ChannelsToPrimaryActor` declares an explicit `@alias(value="Channels to Primary Actor", type=AliasType.LITERAL)` matching this exact (lowercase 'to') heading, overriding `space_separated_name`'s title-cased default derivation.

channels_to_secondary_actors.description: H3 'Channels to Secondary Actors' (optional). How secondary actors interact with the system. Same explicit-`@alias` treatment as `channels_to_primary_actor` above.

related_use_cases.description: H3 'Related Use Cases' (optional). Free-text bullet list linking to parent/child use cases (e.g. 'Superordinate: ...', 'Subordinate: ...'). Unlike v1's typed `{superordinate, subordinate}` split, v2's `RelatedUseCases.items` is an untyped `list[MarkdownListItem]` -- represented here as a flat array of raw item strings, parsed on demand by a caller if the superordinate/subordinate split is needed.

main_success_scenario.description: Body of the H2 'Main Success Scenario' section: a single real CommonMark ordered list.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps, in list order (position is the step's 1-based number -- v2 has no separate `number` field, unlike v1's `Step.number`). `MainSuccessScenario.steps` is `list[MarkdownListItem]` with no declared sub-fields (a 'leaf' list item), so each array entry is a step's *complete* raw content verbatim, including any nested continuation paragraph/sub-list it may contain (e.g. the reference document's step 3, which nests an explanatory paragraph plus a 3-item bullet list beneath its own leading sentence) -- not just its first line.

extensions.description: Body of the optional H2 'Extensions' section.

intro.description: An optional leading paragraph directly under the 'Extensions' h2, before any 'Extension N.' h3 sub-heading. Absent (`null`) in the reference document.

extensions.description: One entry per dynamically-named 'Extension {ref}. {condition}' h3 sub-heading (matched via `Extension`'s regex `@alias`, `^Extension \d+[a-z]?\. .+$`). Named `extensions` (same as the parent object's own top-level key) because it mirrors `uc.models.v2.use_case.Extensions.extensions: list[Extension] | None` exactly.

items.description: One 'Extension {ref}. {condition}' h3 sub-section. `reference`/`condition` are derived from the heading text (`Extension.text`), not separate declared Pydantic fields -- `UseCase.validate_step_references_resolve_and_are_unique` (Task 1.6) extracts `reference` the same way, via `_EXTENSION_HEADING_PATTERN`.

heading.description: The h3 heading's full, verbatim text, e.g. "Extension 3a. Company is out of one of the ordered items".

reference.description: The heading's `{ref}` group, e.g. "3a". Its leading digits must resolve to an existing 1-based position in `main_success_scenario.steps`; the trailing letter (if any) is never itself checked. Must be unique among all `extensions[].reference` values in the document.

condition.description: The heading's `{condition}` group, e.g. "Company is out of one of the ordered items".

actions.description: The h3's own CommonMark ordered list of actions (no compound sub-numbering, unlike v1/pre-DEC-010 -- cross-references to the main scenario, e.g. "Return to step 4.", are expressed as plain prose inside an action's own text, not encoded in the list marker).

items.description: One `ExtensionItem`: `text` is the action's own leading paragraph (verbatim, marker-free); `notes` is populated only when the action has a genuine block-level continuation paragraph (a *loose*-list blank line before the next block) -- a same-paragraph soft line break (as in the reference document's own Extension 3a, action 1) stays part of `text` instead.

notes.description: Optional continuation paragraph(s) following the action's leading paragraph, inside the same list item.

sub_variations.description: Body of the optional H2 'Sub-Variations' section.

One entry per dynamically-named 'Step {N}: {label}' h3 sub-heading (matched via `SubVariation`'s regex `@alias`, `^Step \d+: .+$`). Named `sub_variations` (same as the parent object's own top-level key), mirroring `uc.models.v2.use_case.SubVariations.sub_variations: list[SubVariation] | None` exactly.

items.description: One 'Step {N}: {label}' h3 sub-section. `reference`/`label` are derived from the heading text (`SubVariation.text`), not separate declared Pydantic fields -- same derivation as `Extension.reference`/`condition` above.

heading.description: The h3 heading's full, verbatim text, e.g. "Step 1: Buyer may use".

reference.description: The heading's `{N}` group, e.g. "1". Must resolve to an existing 1-based position in `main_success_scenario.steps` and be unique among all `sub_variations[].reference` values in the document.

label.description: The heading's `{label}` group, e.g. "Buyer may use".

variations.description: The h3's own bullet list of alternative ways to perform the referenced step -- a flat `list[MarkdownListItem]` (unlike `Extension.items`, no `text`/`notes` split).

open_issues.description: Body of the optional H2 'Open Issues' section.

items.description: Flat bullet list of open questions/decisions awaiting resolution.

related_information.description: Body of the optional H2 'Related Information' section. Unlike v1 (flat `notes`/`assumptions` arrays directly on this object), v2 models each as its own h3 sub-section wrapping an `items` list -- one extra level of nesting versus v1's own `uc_schema.json`.

items.description: Additional notes about the use case.
Assumptions made in this use case.
